revenue_segments.commentary: Net income 5,311 (+3%) and ROE 34%. Card Services & Auto revenue rose 12% on higher revolving balances and auto operating lease income. Noninterest expense rose 13% on marketing, technology and lease depreciation. Card NCO rate was 3.34%.

revenue_segments.name: Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB)
revenue_segments.commentary: Net income 9,678 (+46%), ROE 22%. Markets revenue 12,078 (+35%), with Equity Markets +86%. Investment banking revenue was 3,902 (+45%) and Payments 5,296 (+12%). Expense rose 18%. Capital allocated to CIB rose by $8.5B in the quarter.

revenue_segments.name: Asset & Wealth Management (AWM)
revenue_segments.commentary: Net income 1,957 (+33%), ROE 48%. AUM of $5.1T (+18%) and client assets of $7.7T (+19%). Average loans rose 18%, driven by securities-based lending. Expense rose 13% on revenue-related compensation and distribution fees.

revenue_segments.name: Corporate
revenue_segments.commentary: Includes the $4.6B net Visa share gain and $763M of equity investment gains. NII fell 45% to 822 on lower rates, and investment securities losses were 395. Treasury and CIO net income was 529 vs 1,121 a year ago. Net income was 4,209 vs 1,695.

forward_guidance.text: Management guidance given July 14, 2026 for full-year 2026: net interest income of approximately $105.5 billion, NII excluding Markets of approximately $96.5 billion (both market dependent), adjusted expense of approximately $107.5 billion (market dependent), and Card Services net charge-off rate of approximately 3.2%. The filing says there is no assurance actual results will match the outlook.

key_risks.description: Capital regulation: the March 2026 U.S. Basel III Re-Proposal would raise the Firm's required CET1 capital by about 6% (based on 12/31/25 positions). Together with the GSIB Surcharge Re-Proposal, the increase would be about 4% versus requirements that take effect January 1, 2028. Standardized CET1 is 14.2% against an 11.5% requirement.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q MD&A, Capital Risk Management – Key Regulatory Developments

key_risks.description: Wholesale credit migration: criticized exposure rose to $50.3B from $48.5B at year-end, driven by Commercial & Industrial (Consumer & Retail, Transportation, Industrials, Oil & Gas). Consumer & Retail criticized exposure rose $1.3B to $9.3B. Real Estate criticized exposure rose to $12.2B.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q MD&A, Wholesale Credit Portfolio – industry exposures; Real Estate and Consumer & Retail detail

key_risks.description: Allowance and macro sensitivity: the allowance weights adverse scenarios for geopolitical and macro uncertainty (weighted-average unemployment peaking at 5.6% in 2Q27). Modeled losses under the relative adverse scenario would be about $1.0B higher for residential real estate, $4.8B for credit card and $5.0B for wholesale versus the central case.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q MD&A, Allowance for Credit Losses and Critical Accounting Estimates – Allowance for credit losses

key_risks.description: Apple Card transaction: a forward purchase commitment with expected closing about 24 months after December 30, 2025. It carries a $2.2B allowance for lending-related commitments, about $106B of related commitments and additional RWA modeling steps. Credit card exposure and future charge-offs will grow when it closes.

bull_case: Quarterly net income of $21.2B (+41%) with ROE of 24% and ROTCE of 29%; even excluding the roughly $5.6B of Visa and equity investment gains, revenue growth was strong in CIB (+27%) and AWM (+19%).
Markets revenue of $12.1B (+35%), investment banking fees +30% and #1 YTD global IB fee ranking, with AUM of $5.1T (+18%) and strong net inflows, showing broad fee-based momentum.

Credit is stable to improving: net charge-off rate fell to 0.66% from 0.73%, nonperforming assets fell 6%, and card 30+ and 90+ delinquencies improved to 1.91% and 1.00% from 2.16% and 1.10% at year-end.

Capital strength and return: CET1 of 14.2% is about 270 bps above the 11.5% requirement, TLAC surplus is $100B, a new $50B buyback is effective July 1, and the quarterly dividend is intended to increase to $1.65 (from $1.50).
Full-year guidance (NII about $105.5B, NII ex-Markets about $96.5B) combined with the asset-sensitive tilt and growth in loans (+10% average) and deposits (+7% average) supports earnings power.
Business momentum: card sales volume +10%, active mobile customers +6%, average Banking & Payments loans +13%, and Payments revenue +12%.
bear_case: Reported 2Q26 results are inflated by about $5.6B of non-recurring items ($4.6B Visa gain, $1.0B equity gains) that are unlikely to repeat; Equity Markets +86% is also a tough comparison.
Expenses grew 15% YoY and full-year adjusted expense guidance of about $107.5B leaves little room if revenue weakens; compensation, technology, marketing and occupancy are all rising.

Standardized CET1 has fallen from 15.1% a year ago to 14.2%, and the Basel III Re-Proposal and GSIB changes could raise required CET1 capital by about 4% or more; the Advanced total capital ratio is now the binding constraint.

Wholesale criticized exposure is rising (Consumer & Retail, Real Estate, Oil & Gas, Industrials), and the allowance rests on heavy adverse-scenario weighting; a deterioration would require reserve builds.

Net interest income excluding Markets grew only 4%, Corporate NII fell 45% and the asset-sensitive profile loses $2.4B per -100 bps; much of NII growth came from low-spread Markets balance sheet expansion.

Balance sheet and risk growth: total assets rose 13% in six months to $5.0T, repo funding is up 59%, VaR increased, LCR slipped to 110%, and there is a $1.3B possible-loss range plus unresolved litigation including political and regulatory matters.

what_to_watch.text: Whether 3Q26 results show a normalized quarter without the Visa and equity-investment gains: compare net revenue (2Q26 reported 57.3B; about 51.7B excluding the $4.6B and $1.0B items) and ROTCE against 29% and 26% YTD.

Progress against full-year guidance: NII about $105.5B and NII ex-Markets about $96.5B (H1 reported NII was 50.9B and ex-Markets 47.0B, implying roughly 54-55B and 49.5B for H2 if guidance is on a comparable basis; guidance basis not specified in the filing).

Adjusted expense trajectory: guidance of about $107.5B vs H1 noninterest expense of 54.2B less 0.3B legal expense (about 53.8B), implying H2 of about 53.7B (derived); watch for any raise driven by revenue-related compensation.
Markets and IB durability: Equity Markets (6.0B), Fixed Income Markets (6.1B), IB fees (3.3B) and the IB pipeline commentary; management notes Markets NII and revenue are market dependent.

Credit trends: Card NCO rate versus the approximately 3.2% full-year guide (2Q26 3.34%, 1H 3.40%), wholesale criticized exposure ($50.3B), Consumer & Retail and Real Estate migration, and the reserve build or release path (allowance ratio 1.79%).

Capital: CET1 versus 14.2%, pace of buybacks under the new $50B authorization versus RWA growth, dividend increase to $1.65, and any finalization of the U.S. Basel III Re-Proposal and GSIB surcharge changes.
Visa C share lock-up expiry (August 9, 2026), subsequent fair value changes in Corporate and VaR impact, and the Treasury and CIO securities repositioning losses.
Apple Card transaction milestones, reserve implications and the interchange trials (September 2026), cash sweep class certification and other litigation developments in Note 24.

Leadership transition: Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh named Co-Presidents (June 25, 2026), with Rohrbaugh now CEO of CCB following Marianne Lake's retirement; watch CCB execution and commentary on succession.

hypotheses_explored.question: How much of the 2Q26 earnings beat is non-recurring, and what is the underlying run-rate?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Roughly $5.6B of pre-tax gains (Visa $4.6B net, equity investments $1.0B) flatter 2Q26 revenue. Excluding them, net revenue is about $51.7B, still up about 15% YoY versus $44.9B, driven by Markets (+35%) and fees. The underlying trend remains strong but ROE/ROTCE and EPS overstate the sustainable level, and the 23.1% tax rate rose partly because the prior-year had a $774M tax benefit.
evidence_quotes: Included a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares in Corporate and $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments in Corporate and CIB.
Equity Markets revenue was $6.0 billion, up 86%, driven by strong performance across products and regions.

hypotheses_explored.question: Is credit quality deteriorating beneath the benign headline net charge-off rate?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Headline credit is benign (Firm NCO rate 0.66%, nonperforming assets down 6%, card delinquencies down), but criticized wholesale exposure is rising, concentrated in Consumer & Retail, Real Estate and Oil & Gas, and the allowance leans on adverse scenarios. Net reserve additions are modest ($149M in 2Q26), so any downgrade migration converting to losses is the key risk to watch rather than current losses.
evidence_quotes: Total criticized exposure, excluding loans held-for-sale and loans at fair value, was $50.3 billion and $48.5 billion as of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025
The Firm's qualitative adjustments and its weighted-average macroeconomic outlook continued to include additional weight placed on the adverse scenarios

hypotheses_explored.question: Does the Basel III and GSIB re-proposal threaten the capital return trajectory?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Required CET1 would rise about 6% under the Basel III Re-Proposal alone and about 4% when combined with the GSIB Surcharge Re-Proposal versus current rules effective 2028. With CET1 of 14.2% against an 11.5% requirement, a $50B buyback, and a dividend increase to $1.65, current capital return looks sustainable, but the 90 bps decline in CET1 from a year ago and strong RWA growth (+$151B Standardized in six months) leave less buffer for acceleration.
evidence_quotes: The Firm expects that the changes in requirements reflected in the U.S. Basel III Re-Proposal and the GSIB Surcharge Re-Proposal, taken together, would result in an increase in the Firm’s required CET1 capital of approximately 4%
On June 24, 2026, the Firm announced that its Board of Directors had authorized a new $50 billion common share repurchase program, effective July 1, 2026.
